subject.title: Cron session accumulation can silently exhaust agent context window — no guardrails or warnings

question: Should this umbrella stay open until both the high-frequency warning and cron-session retention slices are resolved, or should maintainers split the remaining guardrails into narrower canonical issues now?
rationale: The source-backed gaps are real, but the warning threshold and base-session cleanup semantics are compatibility-sensitive product choices rather than one safe automatic fix.

options.title: Keep Open For Linked Slices
options.body: Use this issue as the umbrella while reviewing https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/76473 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/90194, then split only leftovers.

options.title: Split Remaining Guardrails
options.body: Create or confirm narrower issues for context-threshold warnings and sessions-cleanup behavior, then let each linked PR close only its own slice.

options.title: Reject Fixed Warning Threshold
options.body: If a fixed sub-30-minute advisory is not desired, close or narrow the warning PR and keep retention cleanup as the primary bug path.

recommendation.title: Keep Open For Linked Slices
recommendation.body: Use this issue as the umbrella while reviewing https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/76473 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/90194, then split only leftovers.

likelyOwner.reason: The hardest unresolved decision is the cron/session lifecycle boundary introduced and maintained in the reaper path.
